_note: THE TEMPLATE REGISTRY. One row per ALIAS SHAPE, never per mission.
A template says what a base quest can express and where its moving parts are. Everything in a
row was READ OFF THE RECORD with `gen_inspect qall <base>`, not inferred, and a row is only
added after its base has been read whole.
WHY THIS EXISTS RATHER THAN A C# FILE PER MISSION: the objective layer is Papyrus-only. Of 245
vanilla Default* scripts exactly one touches SetObjectiveDisplayed. So a multi-beat Delve cannot
show its own objectives from records alone, and the only quests that can are ones driven by a
script that already does it. The `driver` field names that script. Choosing a template is
choosing which driver runs the mission, and that is the thing that cannot be authored from data.
TOKENS: a recipe writes <Place> and <Planet>. The generator maps them onto whatever this base
happens to call its aliases, so prose is portable across templates and an author never has to
know that one base says DungeonLocation and another says TargetLocation.

_shape: Pick something up at one marker, carry it to another, hand it over. The driver displays
objective 10 on quest start, gives the player CargoObject on the first activation, displays
objective 20, dresses the second target, and on the second activation REQUIRES the player to
be carrying the cargo before it completes. Without it, FailMessage shows and nothing moves.
THE BASE SHIPS IT ACROSS TWO POIs and this template collapses it into one: both beat markers
are pointed at the same place alias. That collapse is the whole difference between a cargo
run and a Delve, and it costs one integer per beat.
_extraBeats: BEATS BEYOND THE DRIVER'S TWO SLOTS ARE INSERTED BETWEEN THEM, never after. The driver
completes the quest on the second activation, so the LAST beat is always its slot 2 and the
FIRST is always its slot 1. Everything in between gets a freshly created beat slot: a marker
alias filling inside the place, an activator create-obj'd at it, a stage carrying its journal
line, and a stock DefaultAliasOnActivate gated on the previous beat's stage.
⛔ AN EXTRA BEAT CARRIES A JOURNAL AND NO OBJECTIVE. The driver displays objectives 10 and 20
and nothing else, and of 245 vanilla Default* scripts exactly one displays an objective at
all. Measured across his own corpus: 237 quests carry one objective, 92 carry two, NONE
carries three. So an extra beat moves the story and not the on-screen marker, and the lint
refuses an objective on one rather than writing a string nobody will ever see.
maxBeats is a stage-numbering bound, not an engine one: extras take 60, 70, 80 ... and must
_collapsedNote: Alias 10 is FinalLocation, the second POI. It is deliberately NOT deleted: it still draws and
still fills, and nothing points at it any more. Deleting an alias is the operation nobody has
proven, and an alias that CANNOT fill makes the whole mission silently not load -- which is
the worst failure shape on this lane. An inert alias that fills costs a draw and nothing else.
cannot: a THIRD OBJECTIVE -- the driver displays 10 and 20 and nothing else, so beats beyond its two carry a journal line and no on-screen marker
a beat that is not an activation -- arrival, death and item pickup need a different driver
a beat AFTER the hand-over -- the driver completes the quest on its second activation
a beat in a second place -- that is what this template collapses away, by design

_shape: JESSICA'S TESTCASE 01 WHOLE: find the load, take it to the centre and find the other half gone,
take it back off whoever has it, return to the centre and finish the job. Four objectives,
which no shipped driver can show, so the driver is ours: FrankyCLI/papyrus/duo_delve_driver.psc,
compiled with papyrus/compile.py into the mod's Data/scripts.
SAME BASE AND SAME COLLAPSE as two-beat-one-place. The base's own driver is REMOVED and ours
put in its place, taking its property values (the cargo item, the gang list, the fail message)
off the entry it replaces rather than restating them here.
_beatSlots: Beat 3 has no activator: the carrier is spawned by the driver at a marker alias this tool
CREATES, into an EMPTY Optional alias also created, and objective 30 points at HIM. Beat 4 is beat 2's slot again, so a recipe
must put beat 4 on the same marker as beat 2 and the lint refuses anything else.
Stages 60 and 70 do not exist on the base and are created with one log entry each.
templates._secondPlace: The base's FinalLocation, re-opened on his ruling 2026-09-24: a recipe may put beat 1 there, so the load is found at another POI and carried to this one. It keeps the base's own GetDistance leash; its markers and theme are written from the recipe.
cannot: more or fewer than four beats -- the driver's state machine is exactly this shape
a beat OTHER THAN beat 1 at the second place -- beats 2-4 are the centre, the carrier and the return to that one centre
staged visibility -- the load and the centre are both in the world from quest start

_shape: JESSICA'S TYPE 2, KEEP IT OR GIVE IT BACK: find a thing with a name on it at one place, then take
it to its owner at a second place OR sell it to a buyer at a third. Walking to one completes the
mission and the other objective closes (hidden, never failed: neither side is the villain). His
ruling 2026-10-08: the choice is made by WHERE YOU GO, not by a dialogue menu; and the third
place, 'time to learn', rather than putting both endings at one site.
SAME BASE as the four-beat template. The find is at the base's second place (FinalLocation, as
duo_delve05), the owner at its main place, and the buyer at a THIRD location alias the build
CREATES by cloning DungeonLocation, so the two endings carry the same distance leash.
The buyer's marker + activator are the owner's slot copied; the buyer's ending is stage 100
copied to 110, so both endings are completing stages with their own recap.
_beatSlots: Beat 1 is the find (stage 50, its journal points at the owner). The offer lands on stage 60
straight after, from the recipe's offer block. Beat 2 is the owner's ending on the base's own
completing stage 100; beat 3 the buyer's on 110, which this tool creates.
cannot: more or fewer than three beats -- find, owner, buyer is the driver's whole state machine
the two endings at one site -- the owner and the buyer must be different places, and the lint refuses overlapping pools
a choice made in conversation -- there are no dialogue trees in this shape, by his ruling

_shape: NO DRIVER: THE STAGES ARE THE STATE MACHINE (his ruling 2026-10-08, proven by gen_stageprobe).
A recipe lists beats by TYPE (use, pickup, deliver); each is a stock Default* alias hook that sets
the beat's stage after the previous step's, plus a few lines in ONE generated fragment script
(papyrus/gen/duo_qf_<id>.psc) bound to that stage. Consecutive use beats sharing a group are done
in any order behind one counted objective. The base's driver is REMOVED; the last step lands on
the base's completing stage 100, which carries the reward. See gen_delve_beats.cs.
templates._beatSlots: Beats 1 and 2 take the base's two marker+activator pairs; beat 3 on clones slot 1. Stages and objectives are numbered by the build from the recipe, not from this table.
